He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]. Dickinson attended [[DeMatha Catholic High School]] in [[Hyattsville, Maryland]]. In high school, he was a [[Jordan Brand Classic]] honoree and the Maryland [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] in 2020, as well as a two-time state champion. Dickinson was named a consensus second-team [[2021 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2021 NCAA Men's Basketball All-American]] as a freshman for the [[2020–21 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2020–21 Big Ten regular season]] champion Michigan Wolverines. During his three years at Michigan, the school reached the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] Sweet Sixteen twice, advancing to the Elite Eight once. He was a three-time [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] (twice first team) honoree, leading Michigan in scoring and rebounding in all three seasons. Dickinson transferred to Kansas as a senior and played two seasons there, being granted a fifth year of eligibility. He was a [[2024 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2024]] and [[2025 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2025 NCAA All-American]] and a two-time first-team All-[[Big 12 Conference]] honoree. He was the first men's basketball player recognized as a consensus All-American at two different schools. During his first year as a professional basketball player he was selected for the [[NBA G League Next Up Game|2026 NBA G League Next Up Game presented by AT&T]]. His NBA G League first-year performance was highlighted by efforts that broke (24) and then rebroke (27) the [[Birmingham Squadron]] single-game rebound record. ==Early life== Dickinson was born to Kathy and Tim Dickinson on November 25, 2000 in [[Alexandria, Virginia]].{{Cite web |title=2021-22 Men's Basketball Roster {{!}} Hunter Dickinson |url=https://mgoblue.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/hunter-dickinson/22256 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220419082311/https://mgoblue.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/hunter-dickinson/22256 |archive-date=April 19, 2022 |access-date=June 11, 2022 |website=MGoBlue.com |publisher=[[University of Michigan]]}} Dickinson's mother, Kathy, played [[volleyball]] for [[Niagara Purple Eagles|Niagara]]. Dickinson's father, Tim, played collegiate baseball at [[Buffalo State University]]. He is a fan of the [[Buffalo Bills]].{{cite web |last=Quinn |first=Brendan |title=Info and intel on Hunter Dickinson's commitment to Michigan and a budding 2020 class |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1476955/2019/12/20/info-and-intel-on-hunter-dickinsons-commitment-to-michigan-and-a-budding-2020-class/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=October 21, 2020 |date=December 20, 2019 |archive-date=May 27, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250527151611/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1476955/2019/12/20/info-and-intel-on-hunter-dickinsons-commitment-to-michigan-and-a-budding-2020-class/ |url-status=live |via=The New York Times}} Dickinson has brothers—Ben, Grant and Jason.
